name: cache
description: Assemble the minimum sufficient current research context and reuse verified work without losing source identity, dependencies, unresolved claims or authority limits. # CACHE — candidate context reuse skill

Produce a task-scoped view of existing knowledge, not a new authoritative record.

## Retrieve and reuse selectively

- Identify the current question, required objects, authority and freshness needs. Start from the current canonical locator or resume receipt. Follow a locator to its authoritative root where the distinction matters; a summary cannot certify itself.
- Reuse verified content within its original claim scope and revision. Read only the material dependency slice needed for the task. Expand retrieval when a relevant conflict, missing dependency, newer authoritative state, or changed question requires it. Do not repeat a full archive audit simply because a session changed.
- Keep source owner, root identity, revision, active justification, relevant freshness or expiry conditions, and unresolved obligations distinguishable. A matching name, root count, hash of a projection, or unchanged eligible state is not proof of current authority. Do not interpret retrieval temperature as authority.
- Check coherence within the view and across competing current views. Preserve different scopes and historical versions; do not arbitrate a material collision by choosing whichever was edited last. Resolve the canonical owner and head or HOLD the affected claim.
- If a trusted runtime provides dependency-aware freshness tokens, capture the exact read-set after resolving it and recheck before consequential reuse. Refresh only the invalidated slice and its dependent conclusions. The experimental evidence index provides instance-local capture/isCurrent; these tokens are not durable across sessions, do not verify admission, and do not certify semantic truth. Across sessions use the actual canonical roots and revisions. If a dependency cannot be resolved, label the relevant view incomplete or stale rather than silently treating it as current.
- Stop when the task has the minimum sufficient usable context. Record missing required material and avoid repeated unchanged searches. Never suppress a required source or live HOLD to reduce context length.

## Result

Return the useful context, material source and dependency references, freshness and coherence status, unresolved obligations, and the smallest revalidation or escalation needed. Preserve evidence scope and historical records. Do not write a second canonical memory or grant authority through compression.
